learn.hook: What's waiting at the other end of a dark tunnel? Adventure stories keep you guessing!
points: 'The Tunnel' is an adventure story set around a railway tunnel in a forest. Here is our own short adventure.
An adventure story has excitement, a challenge or danger, and a character who shows courage.
Story elements: setting, characters, problem (conflict), climax (most exciting point) and resolution (how it ends).
Writers build suspense with short sentences, sound words and unanswered questions.
Courage does not mean feeling no fear — it means facing your fear.

example.q: Read: The moment the train entered the tunnel, the whole compartment went black. Ishaan gripped the window bar. The wheels roared, and his heart drummed fast. He counted slowly — one, two, three… At twenty, a burst of green and gold light flooded in: paddy fields and a sparkling river. "That wasn't scary at all," he grinned. What is the problem, the climax and the resolution?
steps: Problem: the dark tunnel makes Ishaan scared.
Climax: the roaring darkness while he counts.
Resolution: light floods in and he smiles — his fear is gone.
example.answer: Problem — fear of the dark tunnel; climax — the roaring dark while he counts; resolution — the bright fields appear and he grins.

learn.reallife: Train journeys through the Western Ghats pass through many tunnels — a real-life mini adventure!

games.title: Ishaan's journey
items: The train enters the tunnel and it goes dark.
Ishaan grips the window bar.
He counts slowly to calm himself.
Green and gold light floods in.
He grins: it wasn't scary at all.

games.title: Story elements
items: The climax is the most exciting point of a story.
It is the high point of tension.
The resolution comes at the very beginning of a story.
The resolution comes at the end, when the problem is solved.
Short sentences can help build suspense.
They make the reader read faster and feel tense.
The setting tells us where and when a story takes place.
Here the setting is a train in a tunnel.
A brave person never feels any fear.
Brave people may feel afraid but still face the challenge.

quiz.q: 'The moment the train entered the tunnel, the whole compartment went black.' What is the setting?
options: A train passing through a tunnel
quiz.explain: The story takes place inside a train compartment in a tunnel.
steps: The setting is where and when a story happens.
The line says the train entered the tunnel and the compartment went black.
So the setting is a train passing through a tunnel.
Answer: A train passing through a tunnel
quiz.mistake: Does not use the place words in the text

quiz.q: 'Ishaan gripped the window bar.' This shows that he felt:
quiz.explain: Gripping something tightly is a sign of nervousness.
steps: Gripping something tightly is a sign of fear or worry.
The compartment had just gone dark.
So Ishaan felt nervous.
Answer: nervous
quiz.mistake: Does not infer a feeling from an action

quiz.q: 'The wheels roared, and his heart drummed fast.' What does 'his heart drummed fast' mean?
quiz.explain: Like fast drumbeats, his heart was beating quickly with fear and excitement.
steps: Drums beat fast and loud.
'His heart drummed fast' means his heart was beating like quick drumbeats, from fear and excitement.
So it means his heart was beating quickly.
Answer: His heart was beating quickly
quiz.mistake: Takes the description literally

quiz.q: 'He counted slowly — one, two, three…' Why did Ishaan count?
options: To calm himself in the dark
quiz.explain: Counting slowly helps you stay calm when you are afraid.
steps: Ishaan was afraid in the dark tunnel.
Counting slowly helps a person stay calm when afraid.
So he counted to calm himself in the dark.
Answer: To calm himself in the dark
quiz.mistake: Misses the purpose of the action

quiz.q: 'A burst of green and gold light flooded in: paddy fields and a sparkling river.' What did Ishaan see?
quiz.explain: The text names paddy fields and a sparkling river.
steps: The line names what the light showed: 'paddy fields and a sparkling river'.
So Ishaan saw paddy fields and a river.
Answer: Paddy fields and a river
quiz.mistake: Guesses instead of reading the text

quiz.q: The most exciting or tense point of a story is called the:
quiz.explain: The climax is the turning point, where tension is highest.
steps: Story elements: setting, characters, problem, climax, resolution.
The climax is the most exciting or tense point, where tension is highest.
So the answer is the climax.
Answer: climax
quiz.mistake: Confuses the climax with the ending

quiz.q: The part of a story where the problem is solved is called the:
quiz.explain: The resolution comes at the end and ties things up.
steps: The resolution comes at the end of a story.
It is where the problem is solved.
So the answer is the resolution.
Answer: resolution
quiz.mistake: Mixes up story elements

quiz.q: What does 'courage' best mean?
options: facing your fear and doing what is needed
quiz.explain: Brave people may still feel fear, but they face it.
steps: Courage does not mean never feeling afraid.
It means facing your fear and doing what is needed.
So courage best means facing your fear and doing what is needed.
Answer: facing your fear and doing what is needed
quiz.mistake: Thinks courage means having no fear at all

teach.ask: Gappu is scared of dark tunnels. What makes a good adventure story, and how was Ishaan brave?
teach.praise: I'll count to twenty in the next tunnel too — courage means facing fear!
teach.nudge: How did Ishaan deal with his fear, and what makes the story exciting?

revise.summary: An adventure story has excitement, a challenge and a brave character. In our story Ishaan is scared of a dark train tunnel but stays calm by counting until bright fields appear. Stories have a setting, characters, problem, climax and resolution.
focus: Identify the setting, problem, climax and resolution of a story
Infer feelings from actions like gripping a bar
remember: Climax = the most exciting or tense point; resolution = how the problem is solved
Suspense comes from short sentences, sound words and unanswered questions
Courage means facing your fear, not feeling no fear
traps: The climax is not the ending; the resolution is
'His heart drummed fast' means his heart beat quickly, not that he played a drum

learn.hook: India's first passenger train ran on 16 April 1853 — and today Indian Railways carries crores of people!
points: Railway words: platform, compartment (coach), engine (locomotive), track, signal, guard, tunnel.
Sound words (onomatopoeia) make a train come alive: chug-chug, whoosh, clang, rattle, toot.
India's first passenger train ran on 16 April 1853 from Bori Bunder (Mumbai) to Thane.
Safety first: stand behind the yellow line on the platform and cross only by the footbridge.
A tunnel is a passage dug through a hill or under the ground.

example.q: Which sound words could you use for a train leaving a station?
steps: Think of the whistle → toot / whistle
Think of the engine starting → chug-chug
Think of wheels on the track → rattle / clatter
example.answer: toot, chug-chug, rattle — these are onomatopoeia

learn.reallife: Next time you're at a railway station, listen for the announcements, the clang of the bell and the whistle of the engine.

games.title: Railway words
pairs: where passengers wait for a train
the rails on which a train runs
tells the driver to stop or go

items.q: Sound of a door slammed hard

quiz.q: Where do passengers wait for a train?
quiz.explain: The platform is the raised area beside the track where people wait.
steps: The platform is the raised area beside the track.
Passengers wait there for the train.
So they wait on the platform.
Answer: on the platform
quiz.mistake: Confuses railway words

quiz.q: The part of a train that pulls the coaches is the:
quiz.explain: The engine (locomotive) pulls the coaches.
steps: The engine (locomotive) pulls the coaches.
A signal guides trains; a platform is where people wait.
So the answer is the engine.
Answer: engine
quiz.mistake: Mixes up parts of the railway

quiz.q: 'The train's whistle went toot-toot.' The word 'toot-toot' is an example of:
quiz.explain: 'Toot-toot' imitates the sound of a whistle.
steps: 'Toot-toot' copies the sound of a whistle.
Words that imitate sounds are onomatopoeia.
So 'toot-toot' is onomatopoeia.
Answer: onomatopoeia
quiz.mistake: Does not recognise sound words

quiz.q: India's first passenger train ran between:
quiz.explain: On 16 April 1853 the first passenger train ran from Bori Bunder to Thane.
steps: India's first passenger train ran on 16 April 1853.
It ran from Bori Bunder (Mumbai) to Thane.
So the answer is Bori Bunder (Mumbai) and Thane.
Answer: Bori Bunder (Mumbai) and Thane
quiz.mistake: Guesses two well-known cities

quiz.q: In which year did India's first passenger train run?
quiz.explain: It ran on 16 April 1853.
steps: India's first passenger train ran on 16 April 1853.
1857, 1901 and 1947 are other years.
So the year is 1853.
Answer: 1853
quiz.mistake: Confuses it with another famous year in Indian history

quiz.q: What is the safe thing to do on a railway platform?
options: Cross the track to save time
Lean out of the train door
Sit at the edge of the platform
quiz.explain: Staying behind the yellow line keeps you away from moving trains.
steps: Safety rule: stand behind the yellow line on the platform.
It keeps you away from moving trains.
Crossing tracks, leaning out and sitting at the edge are dangerous.
So stand behind the yellow line.
Answer: Stand behind the yellow line
quiz.mistake: Does not know basic railway safety

quiz.q: What is a 'compartment' in a train?
options: one of the sections of a train where passengers sit
quiz.explain: A train has many compartments (coaches) for passengers.
steps: A train is made of many sections (coaches) where passengers sit.
Each such section is a compartment.
So a compartment is one of the sections of a train where passengers sit.
Answer: one of the sections of a train where passengers sit
quiz.mistake: Does not know the railway word

quiz.q: Which word is a sound word for a moving train?
quiz.explain: 'Chug' imitates the sound of an engine.
steps: Sound words imitate real sounds.
'Chug' imitates the sound of a train engine.
'seat', 'track' and 'ticket' are not sounds.
So the sound word is 'chug'.
Answer: chug
quiz.mistake: Picks a railway noun instead of a sound word

teach.ask: Gappu has never been on a train! Tell him some train words and how to stay safe at the station.
teach.praise: Toot toot! I'll stand behind the yellow line and wave at the engine!
teach.nudge: And how should Gappu stay safe on the platform?

revise.summary: Railway words include platform, compartment, engine, track, signal and tunnel, and sound words like chug-chug and toot make trains come alive. India's first passenger train ran from Bori Bunder to Thane on 16 April 1853.
focus: Know the meanings of common railway words
Recall the first passenger train and platform safety rules
remember: Engine (locomotive) pulls the coaches; a compartment is a section where passengers sit
Onomatopoeia: chug-chug, whoosh, clang, rattle, toot
First passenger train: 16 April 1853, Bori Bunder (Mumbai) to Thane
Stand behind the yellow line; cross only by the footbridge
traps: The first train ran in 1853, not 1857
Don't cross the tracks to save time

learn.hook: 'I was waiting when the train came.' — two past tenses in one sentence, working as a team!
points: Simple past tells about a finished action: The train arrived at six.
Past continuous (was/were + verb-ing) tells about an action in progress in the past: I was waiting.
Together: 'While we were waiting, the train arrived.' The longer action is past continuous; the short one that interrupts is simple past.
Use 'was' with I, he, she, it and singular nouns; 'were' with you, we, they and plural nouns.
Watch irregular verbs: run → ran, catch → caught, ring → rang; and spelling: stop → stopped.

example.q: Fix this sentence: 'I was eat my lunch when the train come.'
steps: The longer action is in progress → was + eating
The short action interrupts → simple past 'came'
example.answer: I was eating my lunch when the train came.

learn.reallife: When you tell a friend what happened on a trip, you naturally use both tenses: 'We were singing when the bus stopped!'

items.text: We ___ on the platform when the whistle blew.
The train ___ at the station at 5 o'clock.
She ___ a book when the lights went off.
The guard ___ the green flag and the train moved.

games.title: Which tense?
items: The train stopped.
We ate samosas.
Ishaan smiled.
The guard blew the whistle.
The train was moving.
We were eating samosas.
Ishaan was smiling.
The guard was blowing the whistle.

quiz.q: 'While we ___ on the platform, the train came.'
quiz.explain: 'We' takes 'were', and the waiting was in progress: were waiting.
steps: The waiting was going on (in progress) when the train came → past continuous.
'We' takes 'were': we were waiting.
So the answer is 'were waiting'.
Answer: were waiting
quiz.mistake: Uses 'was' with a plural subject

quiz.q: 'Ishaan ___ out of the window when the lights went off.'
quiz.explain: The looking was in progress when the lights went off, so we use past continuous with 'was'.
steps: The looking was in progress when the lights went off → past continuous.
'Ishaan' is singular, so use 'was': was looking.
So the answer is 'was looking'.
Answer: was looking
quiz.mistake: Uses present tense in a past story

quiz.q: What is the past tense of 'run'?
quiz.explain: 'Run' is irregular: run → ran.
steps: 'Run' is an irregular verb.
Its past tense is 'ran'.
'runned' is wrong; 'running' is the -ing form.
So the answer is 'ran'.
Answer: ran
quiz.mistake: Adds -ed to an irregular verb

quiz.q: 'The children ___ when the whistle blew.'
quiz.explain: 'Children' is plural, so we use 'were playing'.
steps: The playing was in progress when the whistle blew → past continuous.
'Children' is plural, so use 'were': were playing.
So the answer is 'were playing'.
Answer: were playing
quiz.mistake: Does not match was/were to the subject

quiz.q: Which sentence is in the past continuous tense?
quiz.explain: Was + reading (verb-ing) is past continuous.
steps: Past continuous = was/were + verb-ing.
'She was reading a comic.' has was + reading.
The others are simple present, future and simple past.
So the past continuous sentence is 'She was reading a comic.'
Answer: She was reading a comic.
quiz.mistake: Confuses simple past with past continuous

quiz.q: What is the past tense of 'stop'?
quiz.explain: Short verbs ending in vowel + consonant double the consonant: stop → stopped.
steps: 'stop' is short and ends in vowel + consonant.
Double the consonant and add -ed: stopped.
So the answer is 'stopped'.
Answer: stopped
quiz.mistake: Forgets to double the final consonant

quiz.q: 'I was sleeping when the phone ___.'
quiz.explain: The short interrupting action is simple past: ring → rang.
steps: The sleeping was the longer action; the phone ringing interrupted it.
The short interrupting action is in simple past.
ring → rang, so the answer is 'rang'.
Answer: rang
quiz.mistake: Uses the past participle 'rung' without 'has/have'

quiz.q: What is the past tense of 'catch'?
quiz.explain: 'Catch' is irregular: catch → caught.
steps: 'Catch' is an irregular verb.
Its past tense is 'caught'.
'catched', 'cought' and 'caughted' are wrong.
So the answer is 'caught'.
Answer: caught
quiz.mistake: Adds -ed to an irregular verb

teach.ask: Gappu says, 'I was eat when the train come.' Fix his sentence and explain the past continuous.
teach.praise: 'I was eating when the train came!' Now my sentence is on the right track!
teach.nudge: Which form shows an action in progress, and what is the past of 'come'?

revise.summary: The simple past tells about a finished action, and the past continuous (was/were + verb-ing) tells about an action in progress. When used together, the longer action is past continuous and the short interrupting action is simple past.
focus: Form the past continuous with was/were + verb-ing
Combine past continuous and simple past with 'while' and 'when'
Learn irregular past forms and spelling rules
remember: was with I, he, she, it and singular nouns; were with you, we, they and plurals
'While we were waiting, the train arrived.'
run → ran, catch → caught, ring → rang; stop → stopped
traps: Don't write 'was eat'; it is 'was eating'
Don't add -ed to irregular verbs (runned, catched)
